### Changed

- Merge both the bundle and app chart into the same repository. Now the AWS EFS Driver app and the bundle containing the necessary IAM resources (managed by Crossplane) will live in this repository.

## Breaking

This release contains breaking changes.

The `aws-efs-csi-driver` chart must not be installed directly anymore, instead users need to install its bundle App: `aws-efs-csi-driver-bundle`, which is installed on the Management Cluster and contains Crossplane resources to create the required AWS IAM resources for the EFS CSI driver. In turn the bundle chart will install the `aws-efs-csi-driver` app on the Workload Cluster automatically.

Refer to the main [README.md](https://github.com/giantswarm/aws-efs-csi-driver?tab=readme-ov-file#installation) file for an example manifest to install the bundle app. Note that before installing the bundle App on a cluster using the new version, you'll first need to uninstall the previous `aws-efs-csi-driver` App.

Here's an example diff of how the App upgrade would look like on a cluster named `foo`:

```diff
--- efs-csi-driver-app-2.x.x.yaml	2025-11-06 14:20:34
+++ efs-csi-driver-app-3.x.x.yaml	2025-11-06 14:32:03
@@ -1,27 +1,22 @@
 apiVersion: application.giantswarm.io/v1alpha1
 kind: App
 metadata:
   labels:
-    app.kubernetes.io/name: aws-efs-csi-driver
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: aws-efs-csi-driver-bundle
     giantswarm.io/cluster: foo
-  name: foo-aws-efs-csi-driver
+  name: foo-aws-efs-csi-driver-bundle
   namespace: org-bar
 spec:
   catalog: giantswarm
   config:
     configMap:
       name: foo-cluster-values
       namespace: org-bar
     secret:
       name: ""
       namespace: ""
   kubeConfig:
-    context:
-      name: foo-kubeconfig
-    inCluster: false
-    secret:
-      name: foo-kubeconfig
-      namespace: org-bar
-  name: aws-efs-csi-driver
-  namespace: kube-system
-  version: 2.1.5
+    inCluster: true
+  name: aws-efs-csi-driver-bundle
+  namespace: org-bar
+  version: 3.0.0
```

Note that a change like the one above will uninstall the old `aws-efs-csi-driver` App and install the new one `aws-efs-csi-driver-bundle`. Also note that the target kubeconfig for the new App is the Management Cluster (`inCluster: true`), that's intentional as it's where the Crossplane IAM resources are created.
